mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% (as of the decision date) signals an extremely accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (as of decision date), or the rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 9.0% (as of the decision date) predicts negative 20-day forward returns because it signals a weak labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing equity sell-offs.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 9.0% (as of decision date), or the rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO above its 12-month moving average) coupled with a falling unemployment rate (UNRATE below its 12-month moving average) signals a strong economic expansion that leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO > 12-month MA and UNRATE < 12-month MA, or the rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 220), the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day forward returns because higher interest rates and elevated inflation expectations reduce equity valuations and increase risk aversion.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 220, or the rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 2% (as of the decision date) is associated with positive 60-day forward returns because strong economic growth supports corporate earnings and reduces risk aversion, leading to higher equity prices.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 60-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when the quarterly GDP growth rate is above 2%, or the rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts rate below 500.0 (as of the decision date) predicts negative 20-day forward returns because it signals a weak housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to equity sell-offs.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 500.0, or the rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO above its 12-month moving average) coupled with a falling unemployment rate (UNRATE below its 12-month moving average) signals a strong economic expansion that leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 5-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO > 12-month MA and UNRATE < 12-month MA, or the rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 220 (as of the decision date) predicts negative 20-day forward returns because it signals elevated inflation that leads to monetary tightening and reduced equity valuations.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 220, or the rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
